requirement:
HC represents a GitHub issue by a stable owner, repository, and issue-number
identity. Reading the node supplies the issue's title, opening post, and
open/closed status as one snapshot. HC computes its fingerprint and formatted
text from that supplied snapshot through `Domain`.

For illustration:

```rust,ignore
struct GithubIssueContents {
    title: String,
    opening_post: String,
    status: IssueStatus,
}

enum IssueStatus {
    Open,
    Closed,
}
```
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes` has these obligations:
- A GitHub issue is represented by a stable owner, repository and issue-number identity.
- Reading the node supplies the title, opening post and open/closed status as one snapshot.
- The fingerprint and formatted text are computed from that snapshot through `Domain`.

None of these has a test. `references` shows no `{test}` or `{impl}` sites for the requirement. The test items I found in `src/sdk.rs` (`domain_formats_supplied_contents_without_resolving_a_replacement`, `habeas_paths_preserve_opaque_segments_and_separate_all_node_kinds`) cover only the existing node kinds: `Requirement`, `ReferenceSet`, `RequirementSelection`, `Definition`, `Source`, `CitationReview` and `SiteReview`. The `GithubIssues` tests in `src/github.rs` cover the `github` tool, FIXME issue states and caching. They do not cover a graph node for an issue with this identity, a title/opening-post/status snapshot, or a fingerprint over it. A search of `src` found no `GithubIssueContents`, `IssueStatus` or issue variant of `HabeasNode`, so the gap is real and there is nothing in `src` for a test to exercise.

The gap is acknowledged. `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a `{fixme}` to `requirements.sdk.habeas.github_nodes`. Its body says stable owner/repository/number identity and retained title/opening-post/status contents have no implementation or tests. That is the same gap, and it names `nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26`, which is open.

Every gap is covered by that one acknowledgment, so the determination is FIXME.
